noveltyJustification: All 16 findings are new to the packet: the two skill files were unread before this iteration, and each finding names a steering device sk-code lacks plus the file:line that carries it.
keyQuestions: How do skills/rust-anything/SKILL.md and whole-app.md steer a coding agent through a port?
ruledOut: Reading the two skill files as reference documentation
Treating the allow versus expect difference as a style preference

label: The skill opens with one completion criterion, call a port done only when gate passes, before any command; sk-code opens with a surface description and a routing table and never says what done means for a Rust task

The skill routes by goal size with two entry points, the unit loop and the whole-app loop; sk-code routes on file extension and a RUST keyword set whose specific terms are all binding technologies, so a request to write a Rust CLI lands on a binding reference set

The skill states its own capability limits before the plan and tells the agent to say so to the user, PHP and C# bridge not supported yet; sk-code never says what its Rust set does not cover so an agent cannot warn before committing to a plan

The skill carries a numbered trap list pairing each port trap with the crate that resolves it, utf16.rs for string offsets, pynum::Num for int-or-float, indexmap where order reaches output, fancy-regex for lookaround; indexmap and fancy-regex appear zero times in sk-code

The skill forbids fixing the recording and gives one sanctioned escape with its own expiry, known-diffs.jsonl with a reason that gate fails once it no longer differs; sk-code has no rule that a failing parity test is fixed in the port and never in the expectation

The skill defines a stop condition for the agent, three changes to port.rs in a row with no matching case means stop editing and escalate to the user; sk-code has no rule about when an agent should stop trying
The skill forbids widening a float tolerance to make a mismatch disappear and forbids shipping a slower port silently; both are anti-self-deception rules and both are absent from sk-code

The skill requires Rust unit tests and says why they are not the proof, cargo test passing with no tests proves nothing because the recorded cases are the proof; sk-code requires cargo test to pass and never distinguishes a passing suite from a proving one

The skill prescribes #[expect(lint, reason)] rather than #[allow] so a stale suppression is flagged once it no longer applies, and sk-code prescribes the opposite; expect appears zero times in sk-code and rust-anything is right

The skill ends with a report contract and a wait, naming what changed, gate output, diff counts, bench numbers and the behavior differences or risks left; sk-code has no report contract and the fourth item is what forces an agent to state what it did not achieve

whole-app.md keeps the app runnable at every step through a Rust front door that owns the entry point and falls back to the original, with the fallback rate as the progress metric that only goes down; sk-code has no incremental-cutover model at all

whole-app.md grills the user with a design tree asked in rounds, each question numbered with a recommended answer worded so yes accepts it, and states that facts are the agent's job and decisions are the user's; sk-code has no interview protocol

whole-app.md names three kinds of noise, values, order and lines, and forbids accepting any silently, with the rule that noise is normalized in the case and never in the port; sk-code has no vocabulary for the ways a golden can be loosened

whole-app.md sequences faithfulness before idiom and re-runs the proof after the rewrite; sk-code's style guide is all idiom and never says idiom comes second when a port is checked against an original

whole-app.md makes the lift a fail-closed gate on a copy that writes back only on success, and turns the steps only the user can do into an interactive cutover.sh with a way back at each step; sk-code has no cutover concept

whole-app.md runs a multi-session protocol where a session claims one unit in MAP.md and the generated PORT_MAP.md is the measured state while MAP.md is the plan and the claims; sk-code has no multi-session state model

direction: Reading the two skill files as reference documentation
reason: They are steering documents whose unit is the agent's next action, not a fact; the findings are about behaviour, not knowledge

direction: Treating the allow versus expect difference as a style preference
reason: expect expires and allow does not, so the difference decides whether a stale suppression is ever noticed

direction: Looking for a Rust app path in sk-code SKILL.md
reason: The one behavioural statement about Rust frames it as a compatibility implementation of a TypeScript oracle, which excludes an app path by construction
